method: An entry is a top pick only if (1) its official page was re-read on 2026-11-01, (2) that page did not show it as closed, and (3) the page showed a specific cash prize amount. Free entry is shown as confirmed only where the page said so. Order is a judgement call weighted toward skill-based, code-assisted competitions with large confirmed prizes; it is NOT an expected-value calculation, because participant counts, win odds and many eligibility rules were not confirmed.

topPicks.title: Metaculus forecasting tournaments (incl. Fall 2026 FutureEval Bot Tournament)
topPicks.headline: Page states "You can participate for free and win cash prizes for being accurate." Live pools: Fall 2026 FutureEval Bot Tournament $50,000; Labor Automation $35,000; POTUS Predictions $15,000; US Midterms 2026 $10,000 (ends in 3 days); ACX 2026 Prediction Contest $10,000; Market Pulse Challenge 26Q4 $7,500; Metaculus Cup Fall 2026 $5,000.
topPicks.analysis: Forecasting is scored on calibrated accuracy and is the closest fit for an AI coding agent that can research, build pipelines and submit many probability estimates. The tournament name 'Bot Tournament' suggests automated participants are expected, but the rules were not read.
topPicks.caveats: Read each tournament's rules for eligibility, prize-split formula and any limits on automated or AI-assisted forecasts. Prize eligibility by residency was not read.

topPicks.title: Kaggle hackathons and paper tracks (ARC Prize Paper Track, Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track)
topPicks.headline: Competitions index on 2026-11-01: ARC Prize 2026 Paper Track $450,000 (8 days to go); NFL Big Data Bowl 2027 $100,000 (2 months to go); Google - The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track $35,000 (11 days to go; listing text: "Submit a Research Paper advancing the state-of-the-art for agentic software engineering").
topPicks.analysis: The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track is directly about agentic software engineering. ARC Prize rules (arcprize.org) require open-sourcing and forbid internet/API access during Kaggle evaluation, which limits how a hosted AI agent can be used inside the evaluated solution.
topPicks.caveats: Free entry and eligibility were not read on the Kaggle pages. The ARC-AGI-2 prediction track is effectively over for new entrants (entry deadline 26 Oct 2026; final submissions due 2 Nov 2026).

topPicks.title: DrivenData — GEMS Prize Challenge (US DOE)
topPicks.headline: The Geologic Enhanced Mapping System (GEMS) Prize Challenge: $300,000 in prizes, '4 weeks left' (index page, 2026-11-01), hosted by DOE.
topPicks.analysis: Largest single confirmed open cash prize found among the ML/data competitions that could be read. It is a hard, domain-specific modelling task suited to long coding-agent runs.
topPicks.caveats: Exact deadline, eligibility (federal prize challenges often restrict residency) and free-entry terms were not read. Open the competition page's rules before investing time.

topPicks.title: Devpost hackathons (open, AI-themed)
topPicks.headline: Open on 2026-11-01: Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026 $1,000,000 (to Nov 18); Codegeist 2026 (Atlassian) $120,000 (to Dec 22); Kiroween 2026 $100,000 (to Dec 04); PayPal AI Hackathon $67,500 (to Nov 12); UGREEN Hackathon 2026 on AI NAS $46,000 (to Nov 16).
topPicks.analysis: Build-and-submit contests that a coding agent can accelerate. Judging is subjective and prize pools are split across many categories, so confirmed headline pools overstate the typical winner's take.
topPicks.caveats: Eligibility (country, age, employer) is set per hackathon and was not read. Some entries show 'non-cash prizes' on the index, so open each hackathon's prize page.

topPicks.title: ESPN NFL Pick'em 2026
topPicks.headline: "58 prizes to be won this year worth $102K across four game modes"; "$1,500 in guaranteed prizes available EVERY WEEK"; $5K bonus for full picks in all 4 modes every week; page says FREE to play, up to 10 entries.
topPicks.analysis: Open, free and requires no technical setup; it is a pure prediction game. Prize money is spread across many weekly and season placings, so any one entry has a small chance at a large prize.
topPicks.caveats: Official Rules (eligibility, state exclusions, rules on automated entries) were not read. Do not automate entries without reading them.

topPicks.title: CBS Sports Pro Football Pick'em 2026
topPicks.headline: Official Rules: 18 weekly prizes of US$1,000 each; US$5,000 season-long prize; US$100,000 contingency prize (every game correct AND exact scores on both tiebreaker games). Free, no purchase. One entry per person; open to residents of the 50 states + DC aged 18+ (or age of majority).
topPicks.analysis: Fully published, free and open to Texas residents under the stated 50-state eligibility. The $100,000 contingency prize requires a perfect week plus exact scores, which is practically out of reach; the realistic targets are the $1,000 weekly and $5,000 season prizes.
topPicks.caveats: Rules chunks 2-5 (legal terms, prize claim and verification steps) were not read.

topPicks.title: Checkmate Gaming free-entry esports tournaments
topPicks.headline: Page: "Totally free to enter with real cash prizes." Free-entry listings on 2026-11-01 (Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, 4v4 SND) show $40 and $120 prizes, plus a '$100 *INVITE ONLY*' 1v1 labelled free entry. The '$1500 ELITE 3v3' is labelled ELITE ENTRY, not free.
topPicks.analysis: Real, free, daily and low-barrier, but prizes are small and are won by human gameplay skill, so a coding agent has no role; using automation in live matches would likely breach game rules.
topPicks.caveats: Regions shown are US/CA/EU. Age, ID and payout rules were not read.

keyFindings: Coverage is the main limit. Only {verified} of {total} entries were re-read on an official page on 2026-11-01 ({unreachable} more are JavaScript-only pages). The other {unverified} are shown with blank values and an Unverified badge.

The old ledger is stale. {verifiedWithDiscrepancy} of the {verified} entries that could be read showed a discrepancy or an unconfirmable figure versus the old ledger: ESPN Survivor and the AIcrowd ARC challenge are closed, the TradingView Leap edition cited is completed, the Metaculus pool named is pending winners, and several prize ranges no longer match (Devpost, DrivenData, Checkmate).
Every ledger row carries the same check date (2026-08-19) — 74 days before this review — so ledger status fields should not be trusted without a fresh look.

"True free path" is over-broad. The old headline counts {ledgerFull} entries as free USD paths, including {ledgerEndedFull} marked ended and 47 whose prize text mentions gift cards, merchandise, trips or similar non-cash items.

Best fit for an AI coding agent: forecasting (Metaculus), ML/data competitions (Kaggle, DrivenData) and hackathons (Devpost). Pick'em games are free and open but cannot be improved much by code, and their rules on automation were not read.
Time-sensitive now: ARC Prize final submissions 2 Nov 2026; Metaculus US Midterms 2026 ends in 3 days; Kaggle ARC Paper Track papers due 8 Nov 2026; NASCAR Fantasy Live registration ends 8 Nov 2026.

repoIrregularities.title: Version labels on the live site contradict the data
repoIrregularities.evidence: index.html header reads 'Pass C · 17 Aug 2026' while assets/data.js declares pass "S", reviewed 2026-08-19; review.html says 'the ledger now runs to 119 listings' while data.js holds 206.

repoIrregularities.title: 'Added this pass: 60' headline is the wrong pass
repoIrregularities.evidence: assets/js/app.js line 134 sets the counter to the length of addedThisPassC (the 17 Aug pass = 60 entries) rather than the latest pass S (10 entries).

repoIrregularities.title: Platform labels are wrong for Android
repoIrregularities.evidence: app.js maps every platform other than 'ios' to 'Browser'; 48 listings include 'android'. Android-only availability is therefore displayed as Browser.

repoIrregularities.title: 'True free paths' headline (189) includes ended and non-cash entries
repoIrregularities.evidence: {ledgerEndedFull} entries are status 'ended' but freePath 'full'; 47 'full' entries list gift cards, merchandise, trips or similar prizes (see section D codes ENDED_BUT_COUNTED_FREE and NON_CASH_PRIZE_TAGGED_FREE_USD).

repoIrregularities.title: Entries stated as 'live' contain past dates in their own text
repoIrregularities.evidence: Examples (status live in the ledger): spie-light ('Deadline 16 September 2026'), crunchdao ('closes 17 September 2026'), ewc-play ('The 2026 edition closes 23 Aug 2026'), draft-pro ('closed 23 Apr 2026' for the NFL draft), plus world-press-photo, weather-potw and epoty (annual contests). Full list: DATE_IN_PAST_REVIEW in section D.

repoIrregularities.title: Single check date for all 206 entries
repoIrregularities.evidence: lastChecked = 2026-08-19 on every listing, 74 days before this review. Live re-checks of {verified} entries on 2026-11-01 found a discrepancy or an unconfirmable figure on {verifiedWithDiscrepancy} of them (see section B), so the uniform stamp does not reflect per-entry verification.

repoIrregularities.title: Policy contradiction: a sportsbook account is listed despite the stated exclusion
repoIrregularities.evidence: data.js header: 'Excluded by policy: ... any contest that requires an account with a gambling operator (bookmaker, sportsbook or real-money DFS)'. Yet fanatics-survivor has signupUrl https://betfanatics.com/ (Fanatics Sportsbook domain) and its rules link is a LegalSportsReport article (third-party, tagged affiliate).

repoIrregularities.title: Source tiers are unreliable
repoIrregularities.evidence: 19 cited sources are tagged affiliate/forum rather than official, 12 entries have no source tagged official, herox.com (the operator's own page) is tagged 'forum', and a PR Newswire press release is tagged official for draft-pro. 3 App Store pages (pickem-sports, sports-predictor, streak-contest) serve as the 'official' signup link instead of the operator's site.

repoIrregularities.title: Superseded documents with conflicting claims remain in the repo root
repoIrregularities.evidence: index.md states 'No KYC/ID verification required to play ... Every entry verified against an official source' (older, 15 Aug 2026) while data.js tags 7 entries Full KYC, 18 tax paperwork and 96 eligibility checks. 100_VERIFIED_CONTESTS.md and 15 AUDIT_*.md files carry different counts. Only data.js is declared maintained.

repoIrregularities.title: Mobile usability (structural observations, not device-tested)
repoIrregularities.evidence: The live page renders all 206 entries as one long list of cards (the page itself says 'No search box, no filters'); it loads three web fonts from fonts.googleapis.com; og:image is the relative path 'assets/og-cover.png' (social previews need an absolute URL) and the file is 1.8 MB.

repoIrregularities.title: 'USD ledger' includes non-USD and non-US-only contests
repoIrregularities.evidence: Prizes in GBP, EUR, AUD and JPY, and 8 entries whose eligibility text restricts them to the UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia/NZ or similar (code POSSIBLE_NON_US_ONLY in offline-findings.json). Not all are usable by a US (Texas) entrant.

repoIrregularities.title: Forex-broker demo contests listed as cash competitions
repoIrregularities.evidence: 14 market entries (e.g. XM, HFM, LiteFinance, Tickmill, FBS, RoboForex, NPBFX, Headway, Deriv, MultiBank, FundedNext, For Traders, BullRush, Trading.com) are broker promotions. The ledger's own hfm-demo prize text says prizes are 'trading bonuses, credited to a live account'. Cash-withdrawability and residency terms for each were not checked here.

repoIrregularities.title: Ledger prose cites forums and aggregators as basis
repoIrregularities.evidence: Several prize/notes fields rely on Reddit threads or ML Contests statistics (e.g. solitaire-cash 'frequent Reddit complaint', codabench/zindi/signate 'ML Contests logged ...'). The stated policy says affiliate/forum sources may be colour only.

repoIrregularities.title: Missing rules URLs and one insecure link
repoIrregularities.evidence: 6 listings have no rulesUrl (aicrowd, codabench, grand-challenge, crunchdao, mlcontests, bundesliga-fantasy); squarespool uses http://www.squarespool.com/.

repoIrregularities.title: No broken internal links found, but external links could not be machine-checked
repoIrregularities.evidence: All relative links in the source repo's .md/.html files resolve. The ledger has 324 unique external URLs; outbound access in the review environment was limited to GitHub/npm/PyPI hosts, so link rot could not be measured. The user-reported broken links are therefore not individually confirmed here.

method_html:
What this site claims, and what it does not.

Rules applied

  • Verified-or-blank. A prize, eligibility, entry-type, date or status cell is filled only if it was read on an official page during this review (2026-11-01). Otherwise it is blank and the row is marked Unverified.
  • Every row has a source link. Where the page was fetched, the link is the page that was read and carries a green checked badge. Otherwise the link is the source the original ledger tagged official (grey not re-checked); if the ledger tagged none, the row is marked no official source.
  • No inference. If a page did not state something (for example whether Kaggle entry is free), the cell is left blank even if it is commonly true.
  • Analysis is labelled. Rankings and AI-agent-fit comments are opinions, shown under an 'Analysis' label, separate from confirmed facts.

How pages were read

  • Live HTTP fetches of the official pages through a text-extraction fetcher. Pages that need JavaScript (Topcoder, Zindi) returned nothing and are recorded as unreachable.
  • Long pages are chunked; only the chunks listed in verified.json were read, and the page list for each entry states which.

Offline audit

tools/audit.js checks the original ledger for internal contradictions (URL form, source tiers, ended-vs-free, non-cash prizes tagged as USD, dates before 2026-11-01). Results are review prompts on the Flagged for Review page.

Not done

  • No entry was entered, and no account was created.
  • Eligibility for Texas residents was not confirmed for any entry beyond the 50-state wording on the CBS and NASCAR rules.
  • External link rot was not measured (see flagged page, section C).

Data and code

ledger.json, ledger.csv, source-ledger.json (unmodified extract of the original), verified.json, and tools/. Source repository reviewed: karagemop466-tech/FreeMoneyApps at commit 466f7c1.
